terms.gloss: the materials of a dish, its ingredients; in Apicius, the mixture made of them
evidence: Apic. 4.5.3: impēnsam ad eās sīc faciēs
terms.comment: Classically impēnsa is outlay, expense; from the first century on it is also what is used up in making a thing, its materials or ingredients (Lewis & Short), and Apicius uses it of the mixture he fills or tops a dish with. Classical Latin has no noun for an ingredient: a recipe names the things and then says haec omnia or ea omnia, and one asks quid inest? or ex quibus rēbus fit?; see the examples.
A word of modern pharmaceutical Latin; Morgan–Owens gives cōnstituentia beside it.

phrases.latin: Ex quibus rēbus fit hoc jūs?
phrases.english: What is this soup made of?

phrases.latin: additō in mortārium saturejam, mentam, rūtam, coriandrum, apium … et cāseum recentem et salsum. ea omnia pariter conteritō
phrases.english: put in the mortar savory, mint, rue, coriander, celery … and fresh salted cheese. Pound all of them together
you will make the filling for them like this

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. ingredients.
